title: The Footnote No One Would Have Checked
script: Wisnu: [thoughtful] Laras, I found something in the paper before submission. One of the citations doesn't actually support the claim I attributed to it.
Larasati: How significant is the claim, in the context of the overall argument?
Wisnu: [carefully] Not central, thankfully, but it's load-bearing enough that a careful reviewer might notice, and an uncareful one certainly won't.
Larasati: So the safer option, practically speaking, is silence. Nobody's flagged it, the deadline is tomorrow, and revising means reopening a section we finished weeks ago.
Larasati: [reflective] I'm not recommending that, to be clear. I'm describing the temptation honestly before we decide against it.
Wisnu: I appreciate you naming it rather than pretending the temptation isn't there. It makes it easier to resist out loud.
Larasati: [honestly] What's the actual source say, then, if not what we claimed?
Wisnu: Something adjacent but weaker, a correlation where I'd implied causation. Fixable, but it softens our third section noticeably.
Larasati: [gently] Then we soften it. A paper that overstates its evidence isn't a favor to anyone, including our own reputations two years from now.
Wisnu: The editor might ask why we're requesting a late revision. That conversation alone feels like an admission of carelessness.
Larasati: [calmly] Let it feel that way. An honest admission of carelessness now costs us far less than a retraction discovered by someone else later.
Wisnu: I keep thinking about how thin the margin was. If I hadn't happened to reread that footnote, this would have simply gone to print.
Larasati: [encouraging] Which is precisely why I don't think this is really about one footnote. It's about what kind of researchers we intend to be when nobody's rereading anything.
Wisnu: Agreed. I'll draft the revised paragraph tonight and send the editor an honest explanation, no softening of that part either.
Larasati: [seriously] Good. I'd rather we be known for correcting ourselves quietly than for being corrected loudly by someone else.
